newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed, Northrop to merge in $11.6 billion deal.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed, Northrop to merge in $11.6 billion deal.

text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp. said Thursday it would buy Northrop Grumman Corp. in a deal valued at $11.6 billion, as consolidation of the U.S. aerospace industry took another giant step forward.

The two companies described the deal as a merger in which the combined Lockheed Martin would emerge as the sole remaining competitor of aerospace giant Boeing Co., which itself is in the process of buying McDonnell Douglas Corp.
The Lockheed-Northrop deal would create a company with annual sales of about $37 billion based on expected 1997 results and a global work force of about 230,000 employees.
The $14 billion Boeing-McDonnell merger was approved by the federal government on Tuesday but still faces hurdles in Europe.
Leaders of Lockheed and Northrop said the merger would help bolster their positions in an increasingly competitive worldwide marketplace.

"Lockheed Martin and Northrop Grumman have been leaders in consolidating the aerospace industry, and we are now taking the next logical step in combining together to shape the future," said Lockheed Chairman Norman Augustine, who will lead the new Lockheed Martin.
Northrop Chairman Kent Kresa will serve as vice chairman of the merged company.

Under the deal, Northrop shareholders would receive 1.1923 shares of Lockheed for each share of Northrop, the companies said in a statement. The deal is expected to close by year-end, pending approval by shareholders and regulators, they said.
After a delayed opening, Northrop stock soared $23.75 to $112.625 and Lockheed fell $2.19 to $101.81, both on the New York Stock Exchange.

The companies said they hoped to account for the merger as a pooling of interests but might be forced to account for it as a purchase. The effect of the merger will be neutral on 1998 earnings but will add to earnings thereafter, they said.
Lockheed Martin, based in Bethesda, Md., was formed in 1995 by the merger of the former Lockheed Corp. and Martin Marietta Corp. With 1996 sales of $27 billion, it has 180,000 employees worldwide.
Northrop Grumman, based in Los Angeles, was formed by the union of Northrop Corp. and Grumman Corp. in 1994. It employs more than 45,000 people and had 1996 sales of $8 billion.
